opening.argument: The segment is framed as a warning for people who receive gift cards, explaining reported tampering methods rather than inviting viewers to purchase or transfer anything. It describes criminals copying card numbers, obtaining security codes, and draining balances after activation, then turns to protective guidance: checking that packaging conceals the account number and avoiding cards with exposed codes. It also advises consumers how to seek a refund if a card has been drained. That combination establishes an investigative consumer-safety report centered on recognizing and avoiding the alleged scheme.

citations.quote: There's a warning for anyone who has received a gift card for Christmas.
Criminals copy numbers off gift cards on public displays.
But there are ways to protect yourself.
Make sure it has good packaging so you can't see the account number without opening the packaging.
If you do receive a card that's been drained, go back to the retailer and say you want your money back.
